definitions:
taco-r2 minor items N17, N18 and N23 (offline). CPU only; reads stored result files and times nothing.

N17  The held-out exact-shape table of the Triton Mamba-1 scan (Table 5; device time, three GPUs): the population it
     is averaged over, the fallback rule for calls whose exact shape has no entry in the training folds, the regret
     under other fallback rules (plain length bucket, no alignment bit; global chunk only) and entry criteria (mean
     per-call regret, as Table 5; mean latency, as the deployment table), and the absolute headroom in microseconds
     over covered calls and over all calls.
N18  The reference CUDA scan's stock length dispatch (RTX 3090, 2360 captured calls), launch-inclusive and in device
     time: (i) the runtime-chunk build at the stock (chunk, threads) pairing, (ii) the rebuilt module's own stock
     dispatch timed as a separate call, (iii) the installed stock binary timed in its own block (Table 6's 6.6%),
     the re-timing ratios of the same configuration across binaries and within the rebuilt binary, and the shape
     tree (held out) on the same basis, with prompt-cluster intervals and latency-weighted shares.
N23  The zero-parameter compile-facts rule of the top-k table, defined from the code that scores it
     (``taco_model_baselines.compile_facts_matrix``), re-implemented independently and checked.

Output: ``taco_r2_baselines_minor.json``.

Usage:  PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m src.experiments.tpds.taco_r2_minor_checks [--n-boot 2000]

pro6000_device.population: all 2360 captured calls; per prompt fold the table is built on the other four folds

vgpu3090_device.population: all 2360 captured calls; per prompt fold the table is built on the other four folds

h800_device.population: all 2360 captured calls; per prompt fold the table is built on the other four folds

N23.definition: Candidates: the six chunks of the default launch table, each at its default (BLOCK_D, num_warps) and one stage. For each candidate the kernel is compiled (not run) for the target architecture and for the call's alignment specialization (L mod 16 = 0 or not; the aligned facts are used when an unaligned variant is missing), and the compiler's resource report gives the registers per thread and the spill store and load bytes. From the registers, the warps and the SM limits it computes the resident programs per SM k = min(floor(regs_per_SM / (ceil(regs / 8) x 8 x 32 x num_warps)), floor(max_warps_per_SM / num_warps), max_blocks_per_SM) (at least 1), the number of programs P = ceil(d / BLOCK_D) x B and the waves w = ceil(P / (n_SM x k)). The score is S(C) = 1e9 x [spill bytes > 0] + w x ceil(L / C) - 0.001 x log2 C; the rule serves the chunk with the lowest score: any non-spilling chunk before any spilling one, then the fewest sequential wave-tiles (waves times time tiles per program), ties to the larger chunk. No timing and no fitted parameter enter the rule; the hardware constants are the SM count and the CUDA occupancy limits.
